study.question: Does allowing different historical value fields to retrieve different events remove a bottleneck that made whole-event query feedback unsuccessful, under the frozen full-data single-pass recipe?
study.hypothesis: Observed limitation: native scalar query feedback lowers click AUC from 0.6557366273 (g1-r0003-native_q0_w0) to 0.6549095683 (g1-r0003-native_q1_w0); combined feedback reaches only 0.6533441923. Source inspection shows each event has one weight shared across six advertisement fields and historical action. Mechanism hypothesis, not an observed cause: this ties evidence selection for fields with different relevance. A joint full-width local scorer producing one weight per original value field can retrieve complementary evidence; context/target/first-read interaction can then update the target query before a second field-selective read. The hypothesis predicts a positive Q effect specifically with untied field weights. Prior trajectory review: compressed exchange peaked at 0.6474582359; preserving attention mass raised that family to 0.6533304082 but remained below DIN 0.6555440824; the raw-value-residual branch peaked at 0.6514672042 and did not rescue it. Native-width replacement recovered quality, but its no-feedback control is best by only 0.0001925448 versus DIN. All are single-seed observations; none identifies projection loss or routing as the cause. No execution failures are present in the supplied trajectory index.

nearest_work.difference: Read archived primary text arXiv:1706.06978v4 lines 216-283, including Eq.3 and unnormalized intensity. Inherit field concatenation, local activation and signed sums. Proposed change is field-specific event weights plus a second context/history-conditioned query; no original DIN reproduction or general originality claim.

Pinned 90bb99a60724e975ec565836266fd86dcad0039d lines 119-278 use projected event tokens and token-specific query projections, attention and sequence/nonsequence FFNs. Candidate instead keeps original value-field coordinates and uses a full-width Dice scorer with field-indexed outputs; no K/V bottleneck or event FFN. Original paper:est detailed text unavailable; benchmark fallback read. Priority versus the original method remains unverified.

Pinned tokenizer/forward/attention lines 117-211 and 257-341 were inspected: joint field/history/target tokens with projected full/sliding attention. Candidate uses two linear-in-history retrieval passes, no joint token self-attention, and erases invalid historical values before scoring. Original paper:tokenformer full text unavailable, so no novelty or faithful-reproduction claim.

Pinned forward lines 113-159 pool history before field/task token interaction. Candidate tests fieldwise pooling with a feedback edge into a second read rather than only post-pooling token interaction. Comparison is architectural source inspection, not local effectiveness evidence.

inherited_components: Native-width DIN field concatenation, 16-dimensional FeatureEmbeddingDict and four Dice task heads from baseline-din
Two shared local reads, field/history interaction MLP, bounded query residual, averaging and direct side-state readout from g1-r0003-native_q0_w0 and g1-r0003-native_q1_w0
Strict masking of historical keys/actions before Dice scoring from the native trajectory
Unchanged second auxiliary side projection and head access, renamed side_update; it does not modulate keys
Field-addressable repeated retrieval as an external architectural comparison from inspected EST benchmark source; no external numerical result imported
study.proposed_difference: Replace the final scalar scorer output with F outputs, F being the number of original item value fields plus historical action (expected F=7). For each read, s[b,t,f]=MLP([q,k,q-k,q*k])_f. D1: p[b,f,e]=sum_t mask[b,t]*s[b,t,f]*v[b,t,f,e]. D0: replace every s[b,t,f] by sum_g s[b,t,g]/sqrt(F), a unit-norm tied combination that uses every output row. This matches expected initial per-field variance, not realized trained scales or AdamW update geometry; tying produces correlated row gradients. A common field-interaction MLP consumes context,target,first read and produces tanh query_delta and side_state; both enter all task heads. Q1 uses target+0.5*query_delta for the second read; Q0 reuses target. No key/value rewrites. All four cells execute both reads and identical modules. Batched per-field dot products preserve original field ordering. Architectural capacity is equal in stored parameters within the factorial; effective routing rank intentionally differs. At six item fields and one action, added dense parameters versus native are (7-1)*(32+1)=198, giving an analytic expectation of 440811 dense and 32234027 total parameters; host counts are authoritative.
predictions: Primary prespecified estimands from full-population validation click AUC A_DQ: field effects A11-A01 and A10-A00; feedback effects A11-A10 and A01-A00; interaction (A11-A10)-(A01-A00). Joint-evolution support requires positive A11-A10 and positive interaction, not merely A11>A00.

Useful quality prediction: at least one D1 cell exceeds both baseline-din 0.6555440824200336 and incumbent g1-r0003-native_q0_w0 0.6557366272629275. A gain below 0.0005 absolute AUC is treated as a small exploratory effect requiring repetition, not a robust improvement.

If tying is the relevant bottleneck, field gains should appear on nonempty histories, with particular interest in the inherited >64 bin (1401885 samples, 50957 positives, 1350928 negatives). Empty histories have exactly zero pooled history in every cell; empty-slice score changes can still arise from different training and do not prove retrieval utility.

Report all four task AUC/Logloss, click Logloss, parameter counts, allocated GPU/wall seconds, processed examples, peak memory, inference throughput and p50/p95 latency. No efficiency claim from parameter counts alone; compare measured quality-cost frontiers separately from the matched-pass contrast.
falsifiers: If A11-A10<=0 or the factorial interaction<=0, this implementation does not support the claim that field-specific retrieval enables beneficial feedback. A D1Q0 win supports investigating field retrieval alone, not co-evolution.

If both field simple effects are nonpositive, field-selective routing has no local quality support under this recipe; retain the prior incumbent. One implementation does not refute all field-aware attention.

If the best D1 cell fails to exceed both historical references, do not claim benchmark progress. If an apparent win disappears under paired seeds/user-cluster uncertainty, keep it provisional or revise it.

Any influence of padded IDs, target action or supplied current labels on forward predictions; nonfinite gradients; incorrect field flattening; or a host resource-cap breach invalidates the attempted comparison and consumes budget.
Field-specific weights staying effectively tied, or scale-matched follow-up eliminating a gain, would weaken the distinct-evidence-selection explanation even if primary AUC improves.
alternative_explanations: Improvement may reflect extra effective output rank, changed field score correlations or gradient conditioning rather than recovery of complementary historical evidence.
The prior native gain may come from extra nonlinear head features, random initialization or sampling variation, not improved sequence modeling; all prior diagnostics were not_requested.
Preserving unnormalized attention mass improved an earlier family, but that factorial does not establish a universal mechanism and raw-value residuals did not rescue the same family.

Absolute slice AUC differences have different prevalence and populations; history-length effects are descriptive, not proof of missing sequence capacity. Existing >64 diagnostics motivate a bin but not a mechanism conclusion.
One-epoch frozen optimization may favor one representation; no extra epochs or learning-rate changes are allowed to rescue this batch.

Official offline feedback may be immature at prediction time; cart/fav/buy labels match user/category/brand within 24h rather than advertisement-specific conversions. Any result is bounded to this inherited benchmark.

With AdamW, tied scorer rows have correlated gradients and adaptive updates; unit-norm score tying does not equalize optimizer dynamics or effective functional capacity. A positive D effect alone cannot isolate semantic retrieval from these effects.
